subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: A straight line meets the coordinate axes at A and B. Find the equation of the straight line when (p, q) is the midpoint of AB.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 22, book p.143. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. PRINTED DEFECT RECORDED: the book's stem ends "when (p, q) bisects." with the object of the verb missing. Only one reading is possible, since A and B are the only two points named and a point can bisect only a segment, so the card is authored on the sensible reading that (p, q) is the midpoint of AB, and question_text says so plainly. No number was changed and nothing was added beyond naming the omitted object. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split gives the first mark for turning the midpoint into a = 2p and b = 2q, and the second for the intercept form and the final tidy. Paper position: Maths-1B Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Answer checked by substitution: x/p + y/q = 2 is satisfied at A(2p, 0) because 2p/p + 0 = 2, and at B(0, 2q) because 0 + 2q/q = 2. The midpoint of those two points is ((2p + 0)/2, (0 + 2q)/2) = (p, q), which is the condition the question sets.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say how you name the two axis points, and what the midpoint tells you about them.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Use the midpoint
steps.margin_note: First mark. A point on the X-axis has y = 0 and a point on the Y-axis has x = 0, so A and B can be written with one unknown each before the midpoint is used.
steps.memory_tip: A point on the X-axis is (a, 0); a point on the Y-axis is (0, b). One unknown each.
lines: Let the line meet the axes at
A(a, 0) on the X-axis and B(0, b) on the Y-axis
= (a/2, b/2).  This is given as (p, q)

recall.must_convey: That A is taken as (a, 0) and B as (0, b), and the midpoint condition gives a = 2p, b = 2q.
accept: take a as a comma zero and b as zero comma b
the midpoint is a by two comma b by two
a is two p and b is two q
midpoint formula vaadithe a two p avuthundi
the intercepts are double the midpoint coordinates
heard_as: a by two comma b by two

steps.why: The midpoint of a segment has coordinates that are the averages of the endpoints, so each intercept is twice the matching coordinate of (p, q).
common_mistakes: Writing a = p/2 and b = q/2, which halves the intercepts instead of doubling them.
Taking A as (a, b), which ignores that A is on an axis.

steps.label: Write the intercept form
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Put the two intercepts into x/a + y/b = 1 and clear the 2 from the denominators. The line exists only when p and q are both non-zero.
steps.memory_tip: Intercept form is x/a + y/b = 1. Two intercepts in, one equation out.

recall.must_convey: That the intercept form with intercepts 2p and 2q gives x/(2p) + y/(2q) = 1, that is x/p + y/q = 2.
accept: x by a plus y by b equals one
x by two p plus y by two q equals one
multiply by two to get x by p plus y by q equals two
intercept form lo pettina answer vasthundi
the answer is x by p plus y by q equals two
reject: the midpoint is a by two comma b by two
heard_as: x by p plus y by q

steps.why: If p or q were 0 the midpoint would lie on an axis, which would force both A and B to the origin, and no such triangle or segment exists. That is why both must be non-zero.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as x/(2p) + y/(2q) = 1 when the tidier form is asked for.
Multiplying only the left side by 2 and writing x/p + y/q = 1.
